That's what Medicaid does though. Half of the program is about taking your tax money to pay for the expenses of the service, but the other half of the program is the government controlling the costs that companies can charge for a service.

For instance, a dental cleaning where I am can be charged whatever the dentist wants to charge. Mine charges $100 for those paying out of pocket (the highest cost) and then in some cases that's partially paid by insurance companies. An example would be an insurance company negotiates a rate of $40 per cleaning at that location. This means the insurance company would pay $40 and in this case let's say the patient has to pay $0. Medicaid patients pay $0 for their cleanings, but the dentist doesn't get to charge the government $100 or $40. They can only charge $20 and by law no insurance company can get a better deal. So the actual costs of service are lower and the tax payer ends up paying $20 instead of $100.

Part of the reason that the services have to cost more from an insurance company is that negotiating pricing for every item, at each location, for every plan, takes a lot of time and energy on the part of both the service provider and the insurance company. There is no way that an insurance company can provide a better rate in the current system.

I should clarify, I don't think putting everyone on Medicaid is the only option. We just need to remove insurance companies from the day-to-day operations of the medical industry unless they can offer something of value to users. At this time, they only cause the prices to be obscured from patients which means they can be inflated. After all, why lower the price on anything if the consumer is obligated to pay and doesn't see the price until after they're in debt?
